attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The antecedent (without Jensen) and the firm outcome (the bubble bursts) are kept. The nearby line saying collapse already happened allows a retrospective reading, but the drafter's forecast reading is reasonable.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'bursts' as a broad collapse of NVIDIA-centred financing and valuations is ordinary. With no deadline, the contract correctly does not treat short-term survival as failure.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's own 12 Nov disclosure shows Huang resigned. This establishes the antecedent only, not whether the bubble burst.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent is met: Huang resigned on 12 Nov. The packet has no evidence of a broad collapse after that, and none of the boom continuing independently. The early-resolution rule is not met and no deadline was given, so the claim stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: The drafter keeps 'all AI startup revenues', 'most of which', the $1.3T figure and the seven-year window. The 'never made sense' framing is opinion.

contract.note: It is fair to treat the 'never made sense' part as opinion and test the factual parts. The net-loss and realised-revenue bases are the contract's choices; the speaker named neither.

evidence.note: From May 2026: 89% of revenue among 34 top startups, per The Information. That is a different population and an earlier period than 'all AI startups' now.
Secondary report of Q3 losses on mismatched bases: OpenAI's adjusted operating loss, Anthropic's operating loss as filed. No matched net-income figures, and nothing on the commitments.

reviews.rationale: The 89% figure comes from an earlier, narrower sample. Losses are reported on mismatched bases. Nothing verifies the $1.3T in non-overlapping commitments or that most of it depends on funding. The packet neither establishes nor clearly refutes the claim's factual parts.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He cites Ramp data but makes the claim himself.

semantics.note: The rates and quarters are kept. 'Appears' softens the demand framing, but the growth figures are stated firmly.

contract.note: Zitron explicitly links demand to Ramp growth figures, so reading demand as customer spending growth is fair. Quarter-to-date tracking is correctly accepted.

evidence.note: Ramp economist, 2 Nov: Q4-to-date spend is trending 15-25%, after S-1 Q3 revenue growth of 46.7% (Ramp estimate 53.3%). This ties Ramp to the reported figures.
Same researcher: price cuts, not falling demand, with usage up. This is about usage, a different metric from spending growth, and it limits a volume reading.
Rothschild gives 47% Q3 and 145% Q2 sequential revenue growth. This corroborates the earlier rates, measured as revenue.
Ramp, October: monthly spend growth of 0.5% for Anthropic. This fits a slowdown but is a different (monthly) window.

reviews.rationale: Ramp's researcher confirms Q4-to-date spending growth of 15-25%, against 46.7%/53.3% in Q3 and 145% revenue growth in Q2. That shows the stated deceleration in spending growth. The same researcher says usage is rising and price cuts drive the pattern, which limits any reading of the claim as being about usage volume.

attribution.note: Zitron's own metaphorical summary in his post.

semantics.note: The firm 'will' is conditional on NVIDIA 'sneezing'. Paraphrasing the metaphor as stumbling, and the harm as hurting ordinary investors, is faithful.

contract.note: The metaphor has no threshold or response window, and the contract invents none. Requiring a setback and attributable harm after publication is reasonable.

evidence.note: U.S. Bank: NVIDIA fell 4.3% on 12 Nov and the broader market held up. This is before publication, so it cannot settle the forecast.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows no qualifying NVIDIA setback after publication, and no evidence attributing harm to retail portfolios. Whether the antecedent has occurred is unknown, so the conditional is not scored and stays open.
